newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Unisys to appeal Czech DefMin decision.
newsitem.headline: Unisys to appeal Czech DefMin decision.

text.p: U.S.-based Unisys Corp on Thursday said it would appeal a Defence Ministry decision to award a 1.3 billion crown information systems contract to a consortium led by EDS Corp and Digital Equipment.
Unisys said it would first appeal the decision, made earlier on Thursday, to the Defence Ministry, and then to the Economic Competition Office if necessary.
According to Czech law, a firm has seven days to appeal a tender decision. Unisys said it would file the appeal "within the week".

In announcing the decision, Defence Minister Miroslav Vyborny said a commission which evaluated bids put Unisys narrowly ahead of EDS-Digital, but the consortium's lower price and experience swayed the ministry to pick the EDS-Digital offer.
Vyborny said that EDS-Digital asked for 1.295 billion crowns for installation of the staff information system compatible with NATO armies, while the Unisys bid was nearly 109 million crowns higher.
The minister said that the tender commission, which rated bids but was not authorised to make any decision, gave Unisys 98.3 points, while EDS came in second with 97.3.
IBM came in the third with 83.9 points, and a Deloitte and Touche unit, IDOM, had 72.4 points.
Last August, Unisys won an original four billion crown supply tender which was later abolished after Czech competition authorities found irregularities in the process.
Unisys said it was "suspicious" that the original tender was abolished and rankings were changed when it won again.
"We consider this decision on ranking in the public tender to not be objective and unjustified and we will surely appeal against it," Unisys said in a statement.
"The price offer of EDS, as opposed to all other bids, does not include prices for all demanded and in the technical part offered components, as the final report of the commission proves," it added.
EDS officials would not comment on the allegations, but said they would hold a news conference on Friday.
Installation of the staff information system is seen as a large step on the Czech army's path to become compatible with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation members in army command.
